A strong start. A deep farming area.

Evaluated 26,211 observed empty village tiles in x > 0, y > 0, not only croppers. Mandatory: no occupied village 10 fields away or closer, with all 317 cells of that circle captured. This applies to every ranking, provisional location and the CSV; the radius controls do not relax it.

Your original resource priorities now have a 2x proximity-decay factor, so closer oases consistently contribute more. The default looks out to 20 fields; the 10-field counts stay prominent.

Fixed server: https://ts7.x1.international.travian.com. Coordinates open only on a click.

Scored circular radius
Ranking method

The report interprets “10x10” as within 10 fields of the village, a circular radius, not a literal ten-by-ten square. Use 10 or 15 fields to see whether a recommendation depends on the outer ring. The count-only view compares volume without a distance penalty. Coordinates use wrapped 401 × 401 map distances, including the mandatory 10-field village exclusion.

Weighted contribution = base resource priority × exp(-2 × (distance - 1) / 10). The original resource priorities still interpolate linearly between 1, 5, 10 and 15 fields; their values stay flat beyond 15. The extra decay has strength 2 on a 10-field scale, normalized to 1 at one field. Every additional five fields multiplies the distance factor by 0.3679. This is not a uniform doubling of scores, which would leave the ranking unchanged.

At 4 fields the base clay/iron priority is 2.25, but its final contribution is 1.2348. Crop at 10 fields contributes 0.1653, versus 0.1216 at 15. The penalty outweighs the old outer wood/crop increase: closer is always better for the same oasis type. Sum these contributions inside the selected radius; oases beyond it contribute zero. Count-only mode instead gives every oasis exactly 1.

Clay/crop and iron/crop count once as clay/iron. Wood/crop counts once as wood. Crop-only includes 25% and 50% crop oases, each counted once. Owned oases, occupied villages and nonsettlement terrain are excluded as targets or settlement sites as appropriate. Oasis animals, combat losses, actual loot, troop investment, resource production, annexation and other players' farming activity are not modeled. These are preference points, not resources/hour, ROI or a guarantee of safe six-minute raids.

Any occupied village at distance <= 10 excludes a settlement, including exactly 10 and wrapped cross-edge distances. Missing tiles inside that circle also exclude it: unobserved land is not proof of isolation. No alliance, ownership or player exemptions apply. Villages farther than 10 may still appear on the larger local maps. Weighted ties use more oases within 10, then more clay/iron within 10, then more within the selected radius, then coordinates. Equal-count ties use total oases within 10, then within 5, then coordinates; resource types remain equal. Only candidates passing this ten-field rule appear in the ranking CSV. The HTML itself needs no companion file.
